lessons: Round 3's BG opponent (2x Typhoid Rats, 2x Somberwald Spider, 2x Mulch) beat my BG deck 2-1 in games of 17-22 turns, faster than the guide's 15-40 turn stall range.
The guide calls BG the best pair, but my 17-land BG deck went 1-2, so crowded BG needs evasive finishers over extra ground bodies.
Round 1's UR games ran 36-37 turns, but I had few evasive finishers and took Ranger's Guile and Ambush Viper twice each; take finishers over tricks and duplicate filler.
Take and play removal over bodies: my UR deck ran only Harvest Pyre, Sensory Deprivation and Blazing Torch, dropping Infernal Plunge, and lost 0-2 to WU's fliers, Abbey Griffin and Voiceless Spirit.
My UR deck's 36-37 turn wins over BG came from a walls-and-grind game, so value evasive finishers like Stitched Drake over extra Armored Skaab.
Red was the deepest colour, but the early black picks Moan of the Unhallowed and Diregraf Ghoul were wasted, so settle red plus a second colour by pick five.
Tonight contradicted the guide: seat 6's BG went 0-3, not 3-0, and WU went 3-0 at seat 3 and 2-1 at seat 7, against the guide's weak-WU rating.
My BR deck went 1-2 in matches, losing in 15-20 and 48-turn stalls, so prefer a green or black evasive finisher over a fourth removal spell.
My 2-0 win over seat 6 came in 27 and 14 turns, where cheap early pressure ended games; hold removal for big blockers and fliers.
Take Voiceless Spirit and Slayer of the Wicked early and often; two of each anchored a WU deck that went 3-0 in matches and lost only one game.
Prioritize cheap removal like Rebuke, Smite the Monstrous, Claustrophobia, and Silent Departure, which kept the board stable in every round, including the 32-turn grind against WU.
Settle into WU once white flows, since its depth let me cut red's Brimstone Volley and the duplicate Rally the Peasants and Spare from Evil; expect long games and value 2-for-1s.
Tonight's BG did not match the guide: seat 6 went 0-3 (not 3-0), seat 2 was BR 1-2 (not BG 2-1), and the three BG decks went 3-6 in matches.
Round 2's 31-turn loss to WU fliers shows the stall problem: main Somberwald Spider and Spider Spawning to break ground-locked boards, not more ground bodies.
Falkenrath Noble and Morkrut Banshee carried my 2-1 BG deck, so take these strong uncommons over filler like Moonmist, Gnaw to the Bone and Altar's Reap, which I left out.

Don't assume your colours are open: seat 1 also drafted red and blue (Pitchburn Devils, Riot Devils, Scourge of Geier Reach, Harvest Pyre) and beat me 2-0, so take contested red playables earlier or pivot.
My UR fliers were too slow: both 0-2 losses went 21 and 22 turns, so prioritize cheap evasive threats and burn that can close games over slow defensive cards like the second Frightful Delusion.
Keep Delver of Secrets out of a two-colour deck when a playable clock is available; I cut it, and the stronger closers that stayed in (Invisible Stalker, Moon Heron) were the cards to protect.
Contradicting the guide: seat 6's BG deck went 0-3, not the 3-0 the guide claims, and lost 0-6 in games to WU and UR fliers and burn, so BG's 67% record is not a lock.
Games stalled 14-27 turns while my deck relied on ground bodies like Markov Patrician and Walking Corpse; take Spider Spawning or evasive finishers like Falkenrath Noble over filler.
My low-curve BG deck ran 17 lands despite the guide's 16-land advice for low curves, and went 0-6; try 16 lands next.
Take Claustrophobia and Smite the Monstrous early as I did, but expect contested lanes: seat 3's WU deck ran both, plus Spectral Flight and two Voiceless Spirit, and beat me 2-0.
Plan for stalls: my 32-turn game 2 loss to seat 3 shows removal-heavy WU boards grind, so prioritize fliers with a fast clock over slow evasion like Spectral Flight.
Keep creature answers in the main: seat 3 ran two Slayer of the Wicked and Elite Inquisitor, so my four removal spells plus Fiend Hunter need backup from Smite and Ghostly Possession.
